Joshi writes that 'the Sub-period IA of Surkotada is to be dated between 2055 B.C. to 1970 B.C. or if we take the earliest date of Period IB, 1940 B.C.', from TF-1305 (earliest IA) and TF-1310 (latest IA), quoting B.C. dates computed on the 5730-year half-life with 1950 as reference year and uncalibrated (Joshi 1974, p. 36). The 1990 memoir repeats this and adds PRL-85: IA 'is to be dated between 2055 B.C. (if not 2315 B.C.) to 1970 B.C. or 1940 B.C. (TF 1295)' (Joshi 1990, p. 62). Joshi adds cross-dating that points earlier: Reserved Slip Ware in IA matches Sargonid levels at Brak and other West Asian sites, 'dated to 2371-2316 B.C.' (1974, pp. 35-36; 2370-2284 B.C. in 1990, p. 61), and he concludes that 'the movement of Harappans to Kutch took place at an early stage by circa 2300 B.C. when Surkotada was established' (1974, p. 36; 1990, p. 63). syntheses.statement: Possehl and Raval calibrate the Surkotada dates and give an average of 2295 B.C. for Surkotada IA, concluding that 'Radiocarbon determinations from Lothal and Surkotada (Table 1) can be used to suggest that the Urban Phase Sindhi Harappans settled in Gujarat, including Kutch, ca. 2500-2300 B.C.'

Possehl also assigns TF-1295 to IA and TF-1304 & 1309 to IB, the reverse of Joshi 1974 and 1990, following Joshi's 1972 article as Joshi 1974 (pp. 36-37) explains.

syntheses.statement: 'The 14C dating for Surkotada yield an effective time-bracket of c. 2100-1700 B.C.' This is for the whole occupation, not the layout phase alone.
syntheses.disagreement: Uncalibrated, like Joshi's figures; it matches Joshi's 1974 summary of the culture 'between 2100 and 1700 B.C.' (Joshi 1974, p. 34) and is later than Joshi's own c. 2300 B.C. for the foundation.
